justifications.durability: the assertion is verbatim containment of the block the generator produces, so a prompt that drops, truncates or swaps its generated example fails; my independent prose-only control confirms the specific defect §23 names (prose naming a field masking a missing block) is closed, and the positive control test_walk_reaches_expected_prompts still pins the walk. A residual shape gap: the parametrised test indexes _model_objects()[model_name], so a future derived pair whose model is not a scanned *Batch class raises a bare KeyError rather than an assertion naming the prompt.

I independently reproduced both: all ten derived pairs pass the verbatim check against current source, and a prose-only rendering (every field name present, generated block absent) passes the old field-membership check and is refused by the new one. The reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite or after_suite arm, so added failures are unmeasured rather than zero.
justifications.fit: commit subject `test(llm): require each prompt's generated schema example verbatim` is conventional and the body states what changed and why; no plan, sprint or version label and no author or AI attribution appear in the message, the test docstring, or the helper names.

justifications.reuse: the test reuses the existing _collect_pairs/_model_objects AST walk and the canonical imas_codex/llm/prompt_loader.get_pydantic_schema_json generator rather than re-deriving the example format — the plan's stated anchoring — and deletes the now-dead field-name helper instead of leaving it orphaned.
justifications.scope_discipline: the reviewed commit e0feeb38f touches only tests/llm/test_prompt_schema_coverage.py and docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/prompt-schema-guard-verbatim-example.html, both inside the declared write paths (which also include docs/figures/jt60sa-discovery-completion/prompt-schema-guard-verbatim-example); the sibling §23 supersede node's file imas_codex/llm/prompts/signals/individualization.md is untouched.
